content: Chapter 6: Aptitude for Magic Power
[img]../image/ph_varukiri01_ill003.jpg

To put it bluntly, the experiment ended in failure. The development team was adjusting the unit and trying to draw out my magic power, but the fundamental problem lay with me, the test pilot. A severe lack of magic power output. With my magic power significantly below the regulated value, I couldn't withstand combat with Gijuu. No matter how much they strengthened the unit or the Magic Converter, it was meaningless if the crucial magic power output was completely insufficient. Currently, my priority should be to increase my magic power output. However, the development team had little know-how regarding magic power.

“You want advice on improving magic power output, huh?”
On the night the experiment took place, I visited Dr. Allison’s office. In the private room, which was merely a partitioned-off section of the hangar, Dr. Allison’s PC and stacks of documents and books were neatly arranged. Most of them were work-related, but there was a single photo frame on the desk.
“I understand your desire for advice, but you know we also have limited know-how, don’t you?”
“I judged it best to rely on the doctors who possess more knowledge than I do.”
“Did you ask Dr. Smith?”
“He said increasing the proportion of Gijuu cells was the fastest way. At the same time, he also said that even if my entire body were replaced, I wouldn’t reach the expected values.”
“...Haa, that man really is...” Dr. Allison let out a deep
sigh, and then offered me some advice.
“I’m sorry, but we have so little know-how regarding magic that I can’t make any predictions. By the way, do you have any solutions in mind?”
“I’m thinking of increasing my training time and switching to a harder menu to make my limbs more my own. …Right now, this is all I can do.”

The reason I couldn’t meet the specified values was that I wasn’t fully drawing out the magic from the Gijuu cells within me. I came up with the idea of increasing my training to make them more like my own limbs. I didn’t expect my method to solve the problem. That’s why I relied on the doctors.
Dr. Allison gave a wry smile.
“If that would solve it, it would have been solved long ago. Alright, I’ll give you some advice.”
Seeing me straighten my posture and listen intently, Dr. Allison smiled.
“It’s nothing major. If we don’t have the know-how, then we should just extract it from those who do, right?”
“Those who do, you say?”
Should I access a specialized agency? But I couldn’t imagine being able to investigate with my authority. Dr. Allison looked exasperated at my confusion.
“Looking back now, I’m grateful for the principal’s whim. …You’re enrolled in a class of Valkyries who are skilled in handling magic, aren’t you?”
You understand by now, don’t you? Dr. Allison’s gaze seemed to say, and I saluted, having gained a clue.
“Thank you for your advice!”

I had almost forgotten due to the academy’s atmosphere, but these girls were Valkyries, the protagonists of the battlefield. They were the ones most skilled in handling magic and possessed the most know-how.
Dr. Allison stood up and placed a hand on my shoulder.
“Extract the information well. And be careful not to alert the principal or anyone else.”
“Yes, I’ll do my best!”
I was determined to acquire the know-how regarding magic, not only for Dr. Allison who gave me advice but also for the development team. However, Dr. Allison had a worried look on her face.
“…Are you really going to be alright?”

To acquire magic know-how, I attended the academy and was taking Class 5’s lessons. I was taking the classes more seriously than usual, hoping to gain some hints, and Louise seemed to notice my unusual behavior. As soon as break time started, she immediately spoke to me.
“Ren-kun, you’re even more serious than usual today. Did something happen?”
Louise didn’t seem to be probing me; she genuinely looked concerned.
“…I want to improve my magic output, so I was hoping to find some hints in class.”
“Ah, I see. But that might be a little difficult, you know?”
Louise looked troubled, so I asked her why.
“Why is that?”
I tried my best to hide my desperate feelings. Louise didn’t seem to notice my inner turmoil. She looked up and explained the Valkyries’ understanding of magic.
“Magic-related classes are held in middle school, you see. By the time everyone graduates successfully, they’ve all met a certain standard. In high school, other subjects take priority.”
“I-Is that so?”

It seemed I wouldn’t gain any magic-related know-how from classes. In that case, I would have to ask someone directly. The next class was about to begin, so I tried to end the conversation, but Louise seemed to want to continue.
“Did a magic-related problem occur, by any chance?”
“…I cannot discuss that.”
“Oh, right. That’s military classified, isn’t it? Then you can’t say.”
Louise nodded repeatedly, then made a suggestion to me.
“In that case, I’ll teach you about magic. It’s just the absolute basics that even middle schoolers know, though.”
“Are you sure?”
I stared at Louise, surprised by this unexpected stroke of luck, and she was beaming.
“Because we’re friends, aren’t we? If you’re in trouble, we have to help each other.”
“Friends…?”
Louise tilted her head, seeing my reaction.
“What’s wrong? Did you not want me to be your friend?”
“No, that’s not it. I’ve had a long military life, so I have few people I can call friends.”
“Is that so? Were you on bad terms with the people in your previous unit?”

I remembered the squad that had been annihilated before I came here. My relationship with them wasn’t bad; in fact, it was good. But infantry units suffer heavy attrition. Making friends was an act that required a certain amount of resolve.
“…They were comrades. And I was taught that it’s undesirable to form a relationship beyond that of comrades on the battlefield.”

I was taught not to make anyone special, as it would dull my judgment on the battlefield. For some reason, I found myself clenching both hands tightly. As I questioned my own actions, Louise smiled a little sadly.
“I see. Infantrymen have it tough, too. I’m sorry, I asked something strange.”
“It’s fine. More importantly, will you really instruct me?”
Louise lightly tapped her ample chest with her fist.
“Leave it to me! I may look like this, but I’m told I’m good at looking after people.”
Louise’s words, kind even to me, an outsider in the academy, had a persuasive power that made me believe they were true.
After school.
Louise was teaching me about magic. The location was the academy library, and even after school, there were quite a few female students using it.
“When it comes to magic, your heart is really important.”
“My heart, you say? Is that about mental strength?”

“Hmm, that’s important too, I guess? But the most important thing is, how should I put it, your motivation? For us, it’s the feeling of ‘I’m going to become a Valkyrie and fight Gijuu!’ that’s important.”
“A matter of feeling?”
This left me puzzled. I had fought Gijuu for many years. It wouldn’t be an exaggeration to say I had lived to fight.
“I’ve been fighting Gijuu since I was an infantryman, though?”
“That’s just fighting, but whether your own will is there is what’s important.”
“…Will.”

Since losing my family, I had lived as I was told. I was picked up by an organization, and in the training facility, I obeyed the adults. After being thrown onto the battlefield, I obeyed my superiors and fought Gijuu. What Louise made me realize was the fact that my own will wasn’t there.
“No, from now on, I will fight with will.”
If simply wanting to fight Gijuu was enough, then it was indeed a matter of mental state. I felt a glimmer of hope, but Louise’s expression was clouded.

“It’s not just about vaguely believing. It’s more like a strong wish from the bottom of your heart, you know? It needs to be a self-driven motivation, not something you do because someone told you to. It… I think it’ll be difficult for you right now, Ren-kun.”
“No way—! …No, I apologize.”

When I raised my voice in the quiet library, the surrounding female students glared at me. Some even looked at me with curious eyes, wondering what was happening, but when I lowered my voice, they seemed to lose interest. Louise told me to calm down.

“I understand how you feel, but this is a matter related to one’s own aptitude. This is about when I was in middle school, but there were many girls who were better than me in terms of grades. However, most of them couldn’t graduate and dropped out. The reason was that they couldn’t draw out magic effectively.”

It was completely different from my childhood. In the facility, grades were everything. No matter how motivated you were, if your grades were low, you were deemed unqualified without question and disappeared from the facility at some point.
“Then, what should I do…?”
As I was now, my magic output couldn’t meet the specified values. That meant the loss of my reason for existence. My expression must have been dark. Louise put her hands together to comfort me.
“D-Don’t get down, Ren-kun. Um… that’s right!”
Louise stood up and started searching for something on the library shelves. She quickly returned with a book in her hand. The title was *A Book to Become Positive*.
“This is for you, Ren-kun, who tends to get down! It’s an excellent solution to become more positive and improve your magic control. If you read this, Ren-kun, you’ll surely be able to handle magic!”
It was true that I couldn’t be described as cheerful or positive. I accepted the book from Louise.
“Will reading this solve it?”
“Yep! It’ll definitely improve your magic control. So cheer up!”

The words she was using seemed subtly different, but I convinced myself it was because the academy and the development team had different understandings of magic. I flipped through the book, then closed it.
“Thank you. I’ll go home and read it right away.”
When I thanked her, Louise blushed and scratched her cheek with her fingertip.
“Don’t worry about it. We’re… friends, right?”
“Y-Yes.”

Being called a friend filled me with a strange mix of embarrassment and happiness. Could this be called youth? As time, which I had no connection to, flowed by, a female student approached us, her loud footsteps echoing in the library. None of the surrounding students reprimanded the noisy girl. I turned my head, and there stood Lieutenant Hayase with a stern expression.
“I didn’t think you’d still be doing something like this. Louise, you never learn, do you?”
Lieutenant Hayase’s gaze was directed at Louise. She was probably here to warn Louise for protecting me, who was disliked in the academy. Louise resisted, looking down.
“It’s my business what I do, Hayase-san. I’m acting because I wanted to help Ren-kun. Please don’t interfere… okay?”

For Louise, Lieutenant Hayase was also a superior, and although I didn’t know the details, she must have been of higher rank even by the academy’s rules, which didn’t emphasize military style. To protect Louise’s position, I stood up and stepped in front of Lieutenant Hayase.
“Lieutenant Hayase, I requested this myself. If you must blame someone, please blame me.”
Lieutenant Hayase’s

gaze at me contained a sense of revulsion. It was the same look as the soldiers who had seen me as an anomaly in various bases until now. It was a gaze that saw me, who harbored Gijuu cells, as filth… no, as an enemy.
“You seem to have tamed him quite well. And you, for that matter… hmm?”
Lieutenant Hayase’s gaze fell upon the book I held under my arm. Her gaze then shifted to Louise.
“I don’t know what you’re up to, but if you keep doing whatever you please, be prepared.”

As a menacing aura began to emanate from Lieutenant Hayase, the female students started to flee the library. Entering in their place was not a female student overflowing with energy… but a woman in a ladies’ suit with a slit. I momentarily mistook her because the aura she exuded was similar to that of a student. The woman, whose long brown hair was tied up, pointed at Lieutenant Hayase as soon
as she entered the library.
“Ah~! Maya-chan is bullying a kid from another class! That’s not right. As a teacher, I won’t allow it!”

She was probably angry, but the aura emanating from her was light. She was just huffing and puffing to show she was angry, but she wasn’t scary. However, it seemed to have an effect on Lieutenant Hayase.
Letting out a deep sigh, she turned her back to us.
“Ohinata-sensei, could you please not say such slanderous things so loudly? I was just trying to help.”
Hearing Lieutenant Hayase’s claim that she was trying to help, Louise muttered in a low voice.
“…That’s so transparent, Hayase-san.”

Fortunately, it seemed the other person hadn’t heard, which was a relief, but there appeared to be something deep-seated between the two. The person who had come to the library was Ohinata-sensei… apparently, she was an instructor.
“No excuses! Maya-chan is Class 3’s ace! So, you have to be careful about your conduct, don’t you? Sensei hates bullying, so I won’t tolerate it!”

My first impression of the Class 3 instructor was that she was as childish as she looked. Lieutenant Hayase seemed to be weak against Ohinata-sensei, as she scratched her head with a troubled expression.
“Easy for you to say. More importantly, do you need something?”
“Ah, that’s right! We’re having a briefing now, so everyone gather in the conference room! Maya-chan, you’re coming with me.”
“Why don’t you just call me on the terminal?”
“No! I was about to call you, but then there was a commotion, so I rushed over and there you were, Maya-chan!”
“Yeah, yeah.”

Lieutenant Hayase used casual language even with an instructor who seemed to be her superior, which I found unbelievable. However, Ohinata-sensei didn’t seem to mind. Speaking disrespectfully to a superior was an unthinkable act for me. The privilege of an ace… Remembering Louise’s words, I keenly felt that the Academy was an organization distinct from the military.
As the two left the library, the remaining female students breathed a sigh of relief as if a storm had passed. Louise stood up.
“Ren-kun, can I talk to you for a moment?”
We had planned to part ways in the library, but Louise invited me, and we headed to the rooftop.

When we arrived on the rooftop, Louise stood with her back to me, stretching with her hands clasped behind her. The wind threatened to lift her skirt, so I stepped in front of her, placing my hands on the safety fence to avoid looking.
“Did something happen with Lieutenant Hayase?”
Louise gave a wry smile and began to talk about her relationship with Lieutenant Hayase.
“…She dislikes me. I guess you could say Hayase-san is very ambitious? So, she seems to have trouble with easygoing people like me.”

Recalling Lieutenant Hayase’s words and actions, she certainly had a strong-willed side. I had seen many proud and ambitious soldiers in the past, and I did feel a similarity with Lieutenant Hayase… I felt it, but when asked if they were the same, I also felt they were different. The difference between the military and the Academy might be a factor, but I couldn’t come up with an answer. It was simply that she and the gentle Louise didn’t get along. Aces seemed to be granted privileges, but seeing the female students cower in her presence, I couldn’t help but feel it was excessive.
Louise came to stand beside me, gripping the fence and hanging her head.
“I was scouted by Class 3 once. The interview went smoothly, but in the end, Hayase-san objected, so the transfer talk disappeared.”
“Is such a thing allowed?”
To be deemed unfit based on the opinion of just one person… To me, it was unusual.

“That’s what an ace is allowed to do. Well, asking for the opinions of the class members during a transfer is something every class does. Likes and dislikes can’t be helped, but it’s rare for it to be this blatant… I guess?”

Something I understood after being assigned to Class 5 was that the female students aimed to transfer into Classes 1 to 4, where they would be recognized as Valkyries and combat-ready. If they transferred, they would be deployed in actual combat, but they would also receive preferential treatment. It didn’t seem to be solely for the treatment, but these girls, having graduated from middle school, were elites. For ambitious female students, a transfer felt like something more significant than a promotion.
“Louise, you’ll be scouted by other classes.”
“Ahaha, thanks, Ren-kun. Even if it’s just comfort, I’m happy. But you know, the reason I was scouted by Class 3 was because Class 3 currently has the most insufficient combat strength.”
“What do you mean?”
“About three years ago, Class 3’s unit was wiped out. They’re rebuilding now. Honestly, for the Class 5 girls, if they had to choose, they’d rather join another class than Class 3.”
In other words, being scouted by Class 3 and then denied a transfer was, for Louise, equivalent to being told she was unfit for combat.
“Well, how should I put it… it was my last hope, you know. Since Hayase-san crushed it, I don’t have any more chances.”
Seeing her give up with a wry smile, I naturally recalled a certain phrase. My nostalgic mother’s words.
“…Look forward and take one step at a time.”
“Huh?”

Louise looked terribly surprised by my sudden murmur. The expression she showed, one I had never seen before, made her look like a different person from her usual self for a moment. Her eyes wide with agitation, she hastily turned her face away from me, looking beyond the fence. It seemed I had made a mistake again.
“My apologies. I just remembered something I was told long ago.”
“Oh, is that so? You said it so suddenly, it startled me. …By the way, who told you that?”

“My mother. It means to advance step by step at your own pace, without being swayed by your surroundings. So, Louise, you should also focus on the efforts you can make now, without worrying about others’ evaluations… No, that wasn’t advice I should be giving right now.”
I spoke the words I remembered, but they applied more to my current self than to Louise. Having lost my reason for being, all I could do now was accumulate what I could.
“That’s a good saying. Yes, it really is a good saying. I… I feel like I want to try harder too.”
Her voice lacked energy, perhaps because she was feeling down, but Louise, facing me, forced a smile.
“Thank you, Ren-kun. Well then, I’ll be taking my leave. Hayase-san’s interference will probably continue tomorrow, but let’s work hard and get through it together!”
“Yes.”
Then, Louise spoke as if remembering something.
“Oh, and also, there’s an important class for you tomorrow, Ren-kun, so be sure to attend.”
“I don’t believe there are any unimportant classes?”
Louise gave a strained smile at my reply, but then her expression changed to that of a mischievous child as she said,
“It’s a class related to magic power. And, for a boy like you, Ren-kun, it might be a fun class.”
“H-huh. I was planning to attend anyway, so unless there’s an emergency, I’ll definitely be there.”
Louise smiled shyly at my answer.
“Be sure to attend!”

Although I was the pilot of the experimental machine, I was also a student in Class 5 at the Academy. Naturally, I had an obligation to participate in the training incorporated into the classes. Personally, as a pilot of an experimental machine, I had a detailed training regimen prepared for me. Therefore, my honest feeling was that I wanted to avoid unnecessary training as much as possible, but as long as I was enrolled in Class 5, non-participation was out of the question. I was also personally interested in what kind of training the Valkyrie candidates usually underwent. However, on this particular occasion, I regretted that I should have opted out.
“Alright, let’s begin warm-up exercises. One, two, one, two…”

One female student stood in front of her classmates, performing flexibility exercises in the Academy-designated swimsuit. The Class 5 students followed her example, loosening their bodies in the same way. The swimsuits the female students were wearing seemed to be high-cut competitive swimsuits. The reason for my ambiguity was that Louise, who was shyly doing flexibility exercises next to me, had just told me. I had little experience using pools outside of training, and I had no knowledge whatsoever about women’s swimsuits. Every time Louise next to me moved her body broadly, her chest swayed and her buttocks were emphasized, making it difficult to know where to look. Even if I looked elsewhere, all around me were female students doing flexibility exercises. As my gaze wandered, Louise gave a shy smile.

“Well, it’s unexpected to be in the pool with a boy in the first place. And swimsuits are chosen for ease of movement, so isn’t it the best environment for boys? …B-but, even though I invited you, I’m a little embarrassed right now too.”

Louise said this while looking at her surroundings, so it seemed the atmosphere was different from usual. Perhaps they were embarrassed because I was there, as many female students were doing their flexibility exercises with their limbs drawn in. And I felt an unusual number of gazes from around me. The swimsuit prepared for me was apparently a pair of half-spats, covering up to my knees. As I did flexibility exercises like the female students, I could hear whispers. I couldn’t make out what they were saying, but I couldn’t shake the feeling that my presence here was wrong.

The instructor, who had also changed into a swimsuit like the female students, put the whistle hanging around her neck to her mouth and blew it briefly, yet loudly. After gathering everyone’s attention, she looked at me and then declared to the female students.
“Don’t get shy and slack off just because there’s a boy here.”
I raised my hand and asked for permission to speak to the instructor, who had given the warning with an air of annoyance. The instructor let out a small sigh.
“What is it, Hifumi?”
“Yes, Instructor. I believe I am unsuitable for this place. I request a separate menu.”
I should not have participated in a swimming class surrounded by female students. When I asked her to prepare another training menu, the instructor frowned, looking displeased.
“You expect me to prepare a separate menu just for you? Don’t flatter yourself. Since you’ve been assigned to Class 5, you will follow Class 5’s rules.”
“H-however, I believe this situation might cause trouble for those around us.”
“It is for us to judge that, not you. Get back to your flexibility exercises.”
“…My apologies.”
When I returned to my flexibility exercises, Louise, who had been puffing out her chest, smiled at me.
“Oh? Could it be that Ren-kun isn’t good at swimming?”
“No, I can swim without any problems. When I was an infantryman, I even trained to swim with my clothes on.”

I was made to train swimming not only with clothes but also with my equipment on. I almost drowned countless times as the instructors splashed water on me. As Louise went into a forward bend, she told me about the importance of swimming.
“Then you should definitely participate in swimming class. There are exceptions, but girls who are good at magic power manipulation tend to do well in swimming class.”
I was surprised by the information about magic power manipulation that Louise shared, as it was unexpected. I had never thought that magic power and swimming had any connection.
“Is that so? So that’s why you told me to definitely attend yesterday.”
For Louise, it seemed like common knowledge, as she stated it as if it wasn’t particularly important.
“That’s right. The feeling of being in water feels a bit similar to manipulating magic power. That’s why girls who are good at magic power manipulation often swim a lot.”
“Thank you for sharing such important information.”
When I thanked her, Louise gave a wry smile.
“Ren-kun, you’re always so stiff. But that’s also a good thing about you.”

When the flexibility exercises were over, my body was loosened and warm. Just as I thought I could now concentrate on the swimming class without any problems, the female students around me started whispering again, looking at my body.
“Look at those scars.”
“More than the scars, it’s his limbs, right? The regenerated parts are a slightly different color.”
“Swimming in the same pool as a monster is the worst.”

For the female students, swimming in the same pool as me, who had Gijuu limbs, must have been strongly repulsive. As I pretended not to hear, Louise placed her palm on my left arm. She began to pat my body.
“…What’s wrong, Louise?”
“Ahaha. I was just thinking you have an amazing body. Men really do have incredible muscles. And you’re covered in scars… Does it hurt?”
Participating in battles against Gijuu inevitably led to injuries. My body was covered in scars, but my regenerated right arm and left leg were spotless and clean.
“They are all old wounds, so they don’t hurt now.”
“I see. That’s good then.”

Saying that, Louise smiled at me, seemingly worried that I might be hurt by the insensitive comments around us. The instructor blew her whistle briefly, then looked at me and Louise, admonishing us with an irritated expression.
“You two, how long are you going to play around! Hurry up and get used to the water, then get in the pool!”
After speaking, the instructor turned her face away from us and began to scold other boisterous female students. Louise chuckled as she watched, which made me wonder what was so funny.
“Is something the matter?”
“It’s just funny because Sensei is also conscious of Ren-kun.”
“The Instructor? She didn’t seem that way to me?”
She was currently scolding the boisterous female students and didn’t seem to be conscious of me. However, Louise, who had known her for a long time, seemed to see it differently.
“I guess you could say she’s more energetic than usual? Since it’s always been just girls, it’s not strange for Sensei to be conscious of you.”
“Is that how it is?”
As I remained unconvinced, Louise grabbed my left hand and pulled.
“Come on, let’s get in the pool quickly. The first ten minutes are free time, so we can play!”
Apparently, we could play for ten minutes to get used to the water. This was very different from the training I had received.
“I understand, so please don’t pull so hard. Louise? Louise, wait!? First, you should splash water on your body—”
Louise pulled me, hugging my arm, and ran. Because my left arm was being hugged, Louise’s chest was pressing against it.
“Louise, your, your chest is—”
Ignoring my words, Louise maintained her momentum and jumped into the pool.
“Here we go!”
As the two of us jumped into the pool, splashing water, the instructor blew her whistle loudly.
“Louise, and Hifumi! Get out of the pool!”

The pool was indoors, and in addition to a standard one, it also had a diving platform and a pool over five meters deep. It seemed that no expense was spared in the facilities to train Valkyries. Once we had finished getting used to the water, the session finally started to feel like training. Everyone swam 50 meters freestyle, then got out of the water and returned to the starting position. They would then jump back into the pool and swim again, repeating the action. The female students who had been frolicking just moments ago now had serious expressions. The instructor held a tablet in one arm, alternating her gaze between it and the female students.

“Your pace is dropping. Don’t think that those who can’t be serious in training can be serious in real combat. Those who are cunning enough to try and conserve energy will see their evaluations drop significantly.”

As if reacting to the instructor’s word “drop,” the female students’ movements changed. Those swimming picked up their pace, and those returning to the starting position also began to run. As I got out of the pool to return to the starting position, Louise, who had swum in a different lane and gotten out earlier, offered me her hand. Taking Louise’s dripping hand, I exited the pool.
“Everyone has become more serious.”
“When they mention evaluations, you have no choice but to try your best. Come on, Ren-kun, hurry, hurry!”

As I hurried back to the starting position, urged by Louise, many students looked tired and breathless. However, among them, there were also female students who showed no signs of fatigue. All the students in Class 5 were candidates who had successfully graduated from middle school. They were fundamentally excellent and recognized as having the ability to become regular members at any time. Even within this group, differences in ability were clearly evident.
As I returned to the starting position and waited for my turn to dive, Louise, who was lined up in the adjacent lane, spoke to me.
“Ren-kun, aren’t you looking at other girls too much when I’m right here? That’s mean~, I’m getting jealous~.”
Although she said she was jealous, Louise was smiling mischievously. She seemed to be enjoying teasing me.
“That’s not it. I was simply curious.”
“About what?”
“To be honest, I was surprised. Everyone in Class 5 has excellent stamina.”

The swimming class occupied two periods, making it longer than usual classes. Although there was free time at the beginning, we had been swimming at a high pace ever since. Even I, who had undergone extensive training, was starting to get breathless, yet many female students showed no signs of it. Louise was one of them.
“We are candidates, after all. If we gave up at this level, we wouldn’t even be able to advance to high school.”
Louise said this as if it were obvious, and to my eyes, she seemed quite relaxed.
“Among them, Louise, you seem particularly excellent.”
“Eh? Are you perhaps flirting with me? Oh, I’m such a heartbreaker!”
Louise made a playful gesture, but our turn came up, and the conversation ended there.
After swimming and a lunch break, in the afternoon, all the Class 5 students gathered in the gymnasium, having changed into their athletic wear.
“Good news for those of you tired from swimming. To keep you from falling asleep during lectures, I’ve inserted a close-quarters combat training class.”

When the instructor explained that close-quarters combat training would be held, the female students openly made displeased faces. I wondered if it was alright for their evaluations to drop, and Louise, who was firmly maintaining her position to my immediate left, answered my question.
“Close-quarters combat training isn’t effective against Gijuu, so everyone just isn’t motivated.”
“Is that so? However, wouldn’t making displeased faces in front of the instructor result in a negative evaluation?”
“If you’re good at close-quarters combat training, you get evaluated in a different way, so many girls have mixed feelings.”
“Is there something wrong with that?”
“…Even for girls who graduate without becoming regular members, if their close-quarters combat training scores are excellent, they can get jobs in departments related to public order maintenance.”
I had heard that there were anti-personnel units that dealt with humans rather than Gijuu. However, from Louise’s tone, it was clear that they weren’t happy about being recognized for that.
“Is that something undesirable?”

“For us who want to become regular members, it’s a post-graduation job for those who couldn’t achieve results. Being able to continue riding a Battle Dress is appealing, but having to deal with humans is… well.”

For them, who had trained to defeat Gijuu, there seemed to be something they couldn’t fully accept. Before I knew it, the instructor’s explanation was over, and training was apparently starting in pairs. Louise turned her body towards me and held up a rubber knife.
“Alright, Ren-kun, let’s train together. It’s okay. I may not look it, but I’m somewhat trained, so even with you as an opponent, I won’t get hurt—”

Louise was about to begin close-quarters combat training with me, but a female student pushed her aside and stood in front of me. She had short hair, was quite well-trained, and had tanned, brown skin.
“Louise, sorry, but could you step aside? I need to educate this former infantryman so he doesn’t get the wrong idea.”
Louise was slightly annoyed by the interrupting female student and warned her.
“Hey, don’t just cut in like that!”
“Just step aside. Or are you scared to fight unless Louise is your opponent?”

The female student held up a rubber knife, but she didn’t seem like an expert. I thought it was a cheap provocation, but I also quietly held my knife in my left hand. Louise looked slightly surprised at my stance. Since I usually used my right hand in Class 5, holding the knife in my left hand must have made it seem like I was slacking off. I held it in my left hand because it was more reliable in combat than my right hand after rehabilitation, but the female student in front of me seemed to have misunderstood it as me looking down on her.
“You’re messing around. You’re just a former infantryman, don’t you dare look down on us!”

The female student took one large step forward… or so I thought, but the next moment, she was trying to slip inside my guard. Even though there was more than two meters between us. I quickly parried the female student’s knife attack. The first thing I felt was her astonishing speed. It wasn’t the refined movement of an expert, but a strike that purely utilized her physical abilities. The female student laughed as I widened my eyes.
“Don’t compare our physical abilities to you ordinary humans.”

The female student seemed confident in her physical abilities, and it was understandable. She certainly had a trained physique, but to me, the female students of Class 5 were slender. Compared to the robust soldiers I had been surrounded by as an infantryman, their muscle mass seemed inferior. However, their movements surpassed those of trained soldiers. I recalled the battles with the attackers. I dodged the female student’s thrusting knife, but it grazed my cheek.
“Fast!”

Watching the female student’s movements, I evaded with minimal motion and blocked her attacks with the knife in my left hand. As I focused on evasion and observed her, the female student became slightly irritated. There was a lot of wasted movement in her body.
“Do you think you can win just by running away? Come at me a little!”

Feeling the female student’s anger grow, I focused on her swift movements. I knew they didn’t prioritize close-quarters combat training, but there was more wasted motion than I had imagined. Her fighting style seemed to be to overwhelm opponents using her physical abilities, which could even defeat robust soldiers, as her weapon.
“What’s wrong? Want to try using your Gijuu power?”
Her provocation made it seem like she wanted me to use my Gijuu power. She probably wanted to overwhelm me after I used it.
“Not necessary.”
When I refused, she made an openly irritated face.
“You mean you don’t even need to use it against me!”

No, she was probably underestimating me, who was inferior to her. She swung her knife, incorporating kicks into her attacks. Her frustration at not being able to finish me off made it clear she was rushing for a win.
“Why won’t it hit!”
If she had fought calmly from the start, she might have had a chance to win. Timing her careless step forward, I also stepped in, killing her momentum and grabbing her arm.
“Damn it!?”

She must have realized her mistake, and I tripped her and applied a joint lock. No matter how strong they were, if they were human, their joints were the same. As I held her down on the floor, the female student struggled desperately for dozens of seconds before giving up and relaxing her body.
“…I give up.”
“Thank you.”

Releasing the joint lock and cautiously putting distance between myself and the female student, she pounded the floor in frustration. My assessment of the female student I fought was that she was inferior compared to the attackers. They, especially the leader of the attackers, were superior in close-quarters combat. I had heard that the attackers were likely former Valkyries, which would be extremely troublesome if they were undergoing daily training. The possibility of them operating as an organization has increased even further.
Other girls gathered around the female student I had defeated.
“What are you doing?”
“Losing to a normal guy is unbelievable.”
The female student, scolded by those around her, shouted in anger.
“Shut up! Besides, I wasn’t even serious about close-quarters combat training!”
Turning my gaze away from the female student making excuses, I noticed Louise was by my side. She was looking up at my face from below.
“Something wrong?”
“You’re amazing, Ren-kun! That girl wasn’t bad at close-quarters combat, but I never thought you’d win so easily.”
Louise seemed genuinely surprised, and this time her expression was serious.
“I did receive training, after all.”
It was surprising to me that the female student I had just fought was highly regarded. It suggested that the Academy didn’t place much emphasis on close-quarters combat.
“It’s the same for us too. And, in terms of physical ability, we’re superior, so I never thought you’d win so easily. You were able to fight during the attack too… Do you have some kind of secret?”
“I don’t have any secrets.”
When I didn’t answer, Louise, for some reason, wouldn’t let me go. This time, as if she wouldn’t let me escape, she kept asking me the same question.
“Did you undergo some special training? Or do infantrymen also have special procedures? I think those movements are so unusual that there might be a secret.”

Giving in to Louise, who wouldn’t let me go, I looked back at the female student I had fought. She still seemed unconvinced, but there was a reason I won. There was probably a difference in the amount of time we had spent training in close-quarters combat, but the main reason was the environment.
“There really isn’t any special secret. It’s just—”
“Just?”
“—the enemies I fought on the battlefield were always Gijuu, stronger than humans. Half-hearted martial arts wouldn’t work against Gijuu.”

For me, who had survived that hellish battlefield, my opponents were always beings stronger than humans. The reason I could defeat the female students of Class 5 was because it was easier than fighting Gijuu.
“If she had been more skilled technically, the outcome might have been different.”

If they had been more serious about close-quarters combat training, it was highly likely that I would have lost by now. Their physical specs were that astonishing. However, Louise didn’t seem to think so.
“…I don’t think it’s simply a difference in skill. Ren-kun, who was able to calmly win in that situation, probably has talent. And it’s probably an amazing talent.”
Talent, huh? I might have been more talented than other soldiers, but even so, I was still helpless against the Gijuu that suddenly appeared.
“My talent is limited.”
If I were stronger… Thinking that, I clenched my right hand tightly, and for some reason, Louise’s eyes widened. Concerned by her reaction, I spoke to her.
“Is something wrong?”
“N-nothing. Well then, why don’t you train with me next? Now that I know Ren-kun is strong, I don’t have to hold back, right?”
Louise showed me her stance with the knife, but I felt more clumsiness than the previous female student.
“Come on, Ren-kun, you too, take your stance.”
“No, well… yes. Then, let’s begin.”
